text: Every year, Indian brands destroy crores of rupees of perfectly good packaged food, because the delivery apps will not take stock that is close to its date. This is Smart-Clearance. Every carton gets a second chance, chosen by AI.

Munchly Foods, Pune. In a Nagpur warehouse, eighteen hundred packets of Masala Chips have forty-seven days left. Every morning, the Smart-Clearance agent checks every batch against the delivery apps' date rules and real sell-through. Today, one batch fails. Priya gets a push notification: thirteen hundred and sixty packets will not sell in time.

Warehouse records are often wrong. So the agent asks Rakesh bhai, the distributor, for one photo of a carton label. Gemini reads the batch number, the best-before date and the M R P straight off the pack. Verified in under a minute.

Now the agent prices every way out. The online marketplace at fifteen rupees a packet. Local kirana shops at eighteen. The brand's own site, a staff sale, a food bank. And the bin, which is not free. Once you count the stock, the GST credit the company must pay back, disposal, and packaging charges, throwing it all away costs twenty-seven thousand seven hundred rupees.

The agent does not pick one door. It fills the best-paying door to capacity, then the next. Five hundred and eighty-eight packets to the shops, seven hundred and seventy-two online. Net recovery, twenty-one thousand seven hundred and seventy rupees, instead of a loss. Priya reads three numbers and taps Approve. Nothing moves before that tap.

Then four agents go to work at once. One posts the listing on the marketplace. One sends thirty-eight shopkeepers a Hindi notification with a buy ten, get two offer. Fourteen of them order by lunch. One haggles with a Hyderabad wholesaler. Thirteen rupees is below the floor, so it counters at fourteen twenty with next-day dispatch. Done. Token paid.
Rakesh bhai's van drops the packs at the shops on his normal round. The Hyderabad lot ships once the balance lands. Every packet, still well inside its date.

For Anita in finance, the paperwork is ready on day three. The tax invoice, the credit note for the shop scheme, the e-way bill check, and the memo that proves the GST input credit stays. Two thousand six hundred and eleven rupees that would have gone back to the government. Kept.

And for Vikram in sustainability, every rescued batch becomes a line in the BRSR report, with evidence an auditor can follow. Two hundred and eighteen kilos kept out of landfill, from one batch of chips.
When the clock is tighter, the doors change. A Mango Drink batch with twenty-two days left goes to shops, to staff, and the last fifty-eight packs to Feeding India. Nothing destroyed.
Smart-Clearance. Built on Google Cloud with Gemini and the Agent Development Kit. Every carton gets a second chance.
